summary: Adds an orderDate (calendar day) to CRM orders: new column defaulting to today, existing orders backfilled from their creation day (UTC), indexed by account+date; the order page shows 'Date: ...' and the orders tables show orderDate instead of the creation date. Users can't set it (no backdating).

statements.why: Additive column with a default and a backfill; no access, money or deletion changes. createOrder doesn't accept orderDate (test in __tests__/orders/service.test.ts).

statements.text: Each crm order page changed in a way plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: True but uninformative: the order page now shows 'Date: YYYY-MM-DD' (orders/[orderId]/page.tsx:36).

statements.text: Crm orders now also store the order date.
statements.why: crm_Orders.orderDate DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT now.

statements.text: Apply prisma/migrations/20261013000000_order_date to your live database before the new code goes live, or pages that load crm orders can fail too.
statements.why: Valid SQL migration (add column + index + backfill); Prisma selects all columns so order pages need it.

misses.what: The date column in the orders lists (orders page, account orders tab, approvals) now shows the order date instead of the created date; for existing orders it's the same UTC day.
The order date is always the UTC day the order was created and can't be edited, so orders created late in the evening in timezones ahead/behind UTC may show the neighbouring day.
